prompt: Once the planner is built, what does the host's server do when a browser asks for `/assets/index-BVi82VJx.js`?
hint: Where does the app's code run?

choices.text: Runs the script and sends back what it printed
choices.why: That is a back end's picture. Nothing in `dist/` runs on the host.

choices.text: Finds the file by its path and sends it
choices.why: Right. Finding a file and sending it is the whole job; the browser runs it.

choices.text: Compiles the TypeScript it came from
choices.why: The build did that before the upload; the source never reaches the host.

choices.text: Starts a Node process for that visitor
choices.why: No process runs per visitor for a static site.

prompt: Put the path of a change from your editor to a reader's screen in order.
hint: Four steps; you do only the first.
items: A commit is pushed to the repository
A machine runs `npm ci` and the build
The contents of `dist/` are uploaded to the host
The nearest copy answers the browser

prompt: Which of these is uploaded to the host when the planner is deployed?

choices.text: `package-lock.json`, so the host knows the versions
choices.why: The lockfile is read by the build machine and stays there.

choices.text: `src/planner.ts`, in case the browser needs the source
choices.why: The source was bundled into the script; it is not deployed.

choices.text: `courses.json`
choices.why: Right. It was copied from `public/` into `dist/`, and only `dist/` goes up.

choices.text: `node_modules/vite`, which serves the page
choices.why: Vite builds; it does not serve anything on the host.

prompt: Right after the `ln -s` line, `node --version` says `command not found`. What is the fix?
hint: When does the shell read its `PATH`?

choices.text: Install Ubuntu's `nodejs` package
choices.why: That adds a second, older Node, which is the next section's problem.

choices.text: Run the `tar` line again
choices.why: The files are there; the shell just has not looked in that folder.

choices.text: Open a new terminal
choices.why: Right. `~/.local/bin` joins the `PATH` only in a shell opened after the folder exists.

choices.text: Reinstall with `sudo`
choices.why: Nothing here needs root, and `sudo` would not change this shell's `PATH`.

prompt: Which major version of Node does this course use?
You choose a virtual machine for this course. Why does the lesson ask for the desktop edition of Ubuntu rather than the server one?

choices.text: Later lessons open the pages in a browser
choices.why: Right. The server edition has no browser, and lesson 6 on drives one.

choices.text: Node 22 only installs on the desktop edition
choices.why: The tarball runs on either; the difference is the browser.

choices.text: The server edition cannot run `git`
choices.why: It can; Git is in both.

choices.text: It uses less memory than the server edition while it runs
choices.why: It uses more, which is why the lesson asks for 4 GB.

prompt: `/usr/bin/node node_modules/.bin/vite` fails with a `SyntaxError` about `styleText`. What is the most useful first command?
hint: The error never names Vite or a version.

choices.text: `npm install styleText`
choices.why: `styleText` is a function of Node's own `node:util`, not a package.

choices.text: `/usr/bin/node --version`
choices.why: Right. It prints v18.19.1, and Vite 8 does not run on Node 18.

choices.text: `rm -rf node_modules`, then install again
choices.why: The packages are fine; the Node running them is the old one.

choices.text: `git checkout .` to undo recent edits
choices.why: No file of yours is involved in this error.

prompt: `npm run dev` prints `Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...` and then an address on 5174. What happened?

choices.text: Vite failed and nothing is being served
choices.why: Vite did not fail: it took the next free port.

choices.text: Port 5173 is reserved for production builds
choices.why: No port is reserved for that; something else was holding it.

choices.text: Something already held 5173, such as an earlier dev server
choices.why: Right. Read the address Vite prints, and look for the forgotten terminal.

choices.text: The firewall closed 5173 and Vite moved on
choices.why: A firewall does not make a port look taken to a program on the same computer.

prompt: A Node built for `arm64` unpacked on an `x86_64` computer fails with `Exec ___ error`.
Why does the lesson install Vite and TypeScript with `--save-exact`?

choices.text: Without it, npm installs nothing
choices.why: npm installs fine without it; it would write a range instead.

choices.text: So `package.json` names one version, not a range
choices.why: Right. `8.3.5` rather than `^8.3.4`, so every machine builds with the same Vite.

choices.text: It makes the lockfile unnecessary to commit
choices.why: The lockfile still pins everything underneath, and it is committed.

choices.text: It moves the packages out of `node_modules` into the project root
choices.why: It changes what is written in `package.json`, not where packages go.

prompt: Every link and the `fetch` in the planner start with `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`. What does that buy?
hint: Think of the last section of the lesson.

choices.text: Faster loading, because the browser caches the base
choices.why: It is a path prefix; it has nothing to do with caching.

choices.text: A different API server for each environment
choices.why: It holds the path the site is served from, not an API address.

choices.text: Protection against links to other sites
choices.why: It is a prefix for the app's own paths, not a filter.

choices.text: The same code works when the site is served from a folder
choices.why: Right. Build with `--base=/planner/` and every path follows.

prompt: Which of these does `src/planner.ts` contain? Choose all that apply.
hint: It is the file lesson 3 can test without a browser.

choices.text: A function that adds a session and returns a new list
choices.why: Right: `addSession`.

choices.text: The code that draws the list of courses
choices.why: That is `view.ts`; `planner.ts` never touches the page.

choices.text: The total of minutes planned and done in a week
choices.why: Right: `weekTotal`.

choices.text: The `fetch` of `courses.json`
choices.why: That is in `main.ts`, which holds the state.

prompt: With the data as shipped, how many minutes are planned in the week starting Monday 12 October 2026?
The build script is `tsc && vite build`. A type error is introduced. What is in `dist/` afterwards?

choices.text: The last good build, untouched
choices.why: Right. `tsc` failed, so `vite build` never ran and wrote nothing.

choices.text: A new build with the error left in it
choices.why: That is what `vite build` alone would do; the `&&` stops it here.

choices.text: An empty folder, since the build cleans first
choices.why: Vite never started, so it cleaned nothing.

choices.text: Only `index.html`, without its script
choices.why: Nothing was written at all.

prompt: You change one word in `view.ts` and build again. Which file names in `dist/assets` change?
hint: The name carries a hash of the content.

choices.text: Both, because every build renames everything
choices.why: Two builds of the same source gave the same names.

choices.text: Neither: names change only when a dependency does
choices.why: Your own code is part of the content the hash is taken over.

choices.text: Only the script's
choices.why: Right. The stylesheet's content did not change, so neither did its name.

choices.text: Only the stylesheet's
choices.why: The word was in the script, so the script's hash moved.

prompt: A colleague copies a new `dist/index.html` to the host but forgets the new `dist/assets`. What do readers get?
hint: Which names does the new page ask for?

choices.text: The new page with the old script
choices.why: The new page names the new files, not the old ones.

choices.text: A page asking for scripts that are not there
choices.why: Right. The names changed with the content, so the page asks for files the host does not have.

choices.text: The old page, because the host keeps it in cache
choices.why: The host serves what it was given, and it was given the new page.

choices.text: The new version, because the browser rebuilds the bundle
choices.why: A browser never builds anything; it runs what it receives.

prompt: Why does double-clicking `dist/index.html` show a blank page?

choices.text: The build forgot to include the script
choices.why: The script is in `dist/assets`; it is the way it is loaded that fails.

choices.text: Browsers cannot display HTML from disk
choices.why: They display it; what they refuse is the module script.

choices.text: The browser refuses a module script from a `file://` address
choices.why: Right. A host speaks HTTP, so the test has to as well.

choices.text: `index.html` needs `npm run dev` running
choices.why: The built page needs no dev server, only an HTTP one.

prompt: In `host.mjs`, what is `normalize(path)` there for?

choices.text: Lower-casing paths, so `/Index.html` finds `index.html`
choices.why: It does not change case at all.

choices.text: Resolving any `..` so a request cannot leave the folder
choices.why: Right. The path is cleaned before it is joined to the root.

choices.text: Adding `index.html` to a folder's path
choices.why: That is the second candidate in the loop.

choices.text: Picking the `Content-Type` from the file's ending
choices.why: That is the `types` table with `extname`.

prompt: When `host.mjs` finds no file, it answers with status ___ and sends the site's `404.html` if there is one.
Which of these does a real host add on top of what `host.mjs` does? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Copies of the files in many cities
choices.why: Right, the CDN.

choices.text: HTTPS with a certificate it renews
choices.why: Right; lesson 4.

choices.text: Running the app's JavaScript on the server
choices.why: The JavaScript still runs in the browser.

choices.text: Rules read from a file in the repository
choices.why: Right: redirects, rewrites and headers.

prompt: Match each host to where its redirect and header rules live.

pairs.right: Nowhere: it has no rules file

prompt: Which of the four hosts cannot build a Vite project from the repository on its own, and needs a workflow you write?

choices.text: Netlify
choices.why: Netlify builds each push itself.

choices.text: Cloudflare Pages
choices.why: Pages builds each push itself, with a Vite preset.

choices.text: GitHub Pages
choices.why: Right. It publishes a branch as it is, or what an Actions workflow uploads.

choices.text: Vercel
choices.why: Vercel detects Vite and builds each push.

prompt: Your team wants a reviewer to click a link and see each pull request running before it is merged, with no workflow to maintain. Which choice fits?

choices.text: GitHub Pages, since it is in the same place as the code
choices.why: It has one site per repository and no previews of its own.

choices.text: Any of Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare Pages
choices.why: Right. All three build every branch or pull request at an address of its own.

choices.text: Only Netlify, because previews need `netlify.toml`
choices.why: Previews work on all three, with or without a rules file.

choices.text: None of them; previews need a server-rendered app
choices.why: A preview is a static build at its own address; the planner qualifies.

prompt: Which three values appear in the steps of all four hosts? Choose all that apply.
hint: The contract between the project and any host.

choices.text: The repository
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The command `npm run build`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A `vercel.json` file
choices.why: Only Vercel reads it, and the planner does not need one to be served.

choices.text: The folder `dist`
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer `netlify.toml` in the repository to typing the build command in Netlify's dashboard?

choices.text: Netlify ignores what is typed in its dashboard
choices.why: The dashboard works; the file is better for other reasons.

choices.text: The file builds faster than the dashboard setting
choices.why: Both run the same command at the same speed.

choices.text: It is reviewed like code and outlives an account
choices.why: Right. A setting in a dashboard lives only in somebody else's database.

choices.text: Netlify charges extra for dashboard settings
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so, and price is not the argument.

prompt: The planner built for `/` is published at `https://ana.github.io/planner/`. What does the browser show?

choices.text: A blank page, with the script missing
choices.why: Right. The page loads and asks for `/assets/…` at the root, which is not there.

choices.text: A 404 for the page itself
choices.why: The page is found; it is the script it names that is not.

choices.text: The planner, working normally
choices.why: Only with `--base=/planner/`.

choices.text: A certificate warning from GitHub
choices.why: The address is fine; the paths inside the page are not.

prompt: For GitHub Pages at `/planner/`, the workflow builds with `npm run build -- --___=/planner/`.
hint: Vite's option for the path the site is served from.

prompt: Built with `--base=/planner/`, the planner works from its front page, but typing `/planner/course/git` into the address bar gives a 404. Why?

choices.text: The base path was not applied to links
choices.why: The links work when clicked, so the base is applied.

choices.text: Course pages need a separate build
choices.why: There is one page; the app draws every screen in it.

choices.text: The host looks for a file called `course/git`, and there is none
choices.why: Right. A click is handled by the app; a typed address goes to the host. Lesson 4 fixes it.

choices.text: GitHub Pages blocks addresses with two levels of folders
choices.why: It serves any depth; it just has no file there.

prompt: Which of these is a limit a static site like the planner is likely to meet on a free tier?

choices.text: The server falling asleep when nobody visits
choices.why: That is a back end's limit; a static site has no process to sleep.

choices.text: Memory used by the running app
choices.why: Nothing runs on the host to use memory.

choices.text: Build minutes, when every branch is built
choices.why: Right. Previews turn every push into a build.

choices.text: The number of visitors at the same instant
choices.why: A CDN serves files to many at once; bandwidth over a month is what is counted.

prompt: Which lesson walks through publishing on a free tier, with a domain?

choices.text: Lesson 4 of this course
choices.why: Lesson 4 writes rules and certificates for the planner; the walk-through is elsewhere.

choices.text: portfolio-project lesson 15
choices.why: Right. This lesson defers to it rather than teaching it twice.

choices.text: front-performance lesson 9
choices.why: That one is about caching headers.

choices.text: Lesson 3 of this course
choices.why: Lesson 3 is CI and previews.

prompt: A site works on Netlify. You move it to GitHub Pages at `/<repo>/` and the redirects stop working too. Which of these explains the second problem?

choices.text: The base path was set wrong
choices.why: That explains missing scripts, not missing redirects.

choices.text: The new host has no rules file to read
choices.why: Right. GitHub Pages reads no `_redirects`, nor any other rules file.

choices.text: The workflow forgot to copy `netlify.toml`
choices.why: GitHub Pages would not read it if it were copied.

choices.text: Redirects need a custom domain on every host
choices.why: Netlify's worked at its own address.
